title: Open, Write, Read: Encoding Windows and the Residue of Reversible Psychosis
content: The ARCH × Φ framework treats biological execution as a conjunction whose product must exceed a threshold, and separates present execution from the persistent substrate that constrains future execution (Rahman, Zorumski & Meloy, 2025; Rahman & Zorumski, 2026). Applied to psychosis, the transient routes—corticosteroid psychosis, postpartum psychosis, metabolic encephalopathy—have carried an untouched designation for that substrate S. This article withdraws it. For each transient route, the perturbing agent is independently documented as a modulator of encoding permissiveness: glucocorticoids gate learning-related spine formation, the puerperium is an oxytocin-, neurosteroid-, and thyroid-defined remodeling state, and the proposed homocysteine comparator latch runs on the kinase cascade that couples synaptic activity to durable change. The central proposal, stated in the series' open–write–read (OWR) cycle, is that the residue of a transient psychosis equals the integral of the durable writing rate across the episode, ΔS = ∫ Φ_N·(A_N·D_N·C_N) dt, so that reversibility is a race between episode closure and window closure rather than a property of the route. Parturition is presented as the clearest endogenous critical period of adult life, and postpartum psychosis as a disorder of execution occurring inside an open bonding-writer, predicting residue concentrated in the mother–infant representational domain rather than in global function. The framework converts treatment speed into mechanistic prophylaxis, defines window management as a therapeutic class distinct from quenching execution, and derives a stratified prediction from autoimmune thyroid dysfunction in postpartum psychosis. Existing null results on maternal bonding are treated as the theory's principal falsification risk and are answered with pre-specified, outcome-independent tests rather than post hoc rescue.
